findings.evidence: The statement applies covariance bilinearity to finite families without requiring one common probability space or square-integrability. Its supplied identity source, lem-variance-and-covariance-identities-for-random-variables, requires square-integrable variables on one probability space; the finite-space variance definition is narrower. Add the common-space and L² hypotheses, or state the finite-probability-space scope.

“Finite family” specifies the number of summands, not a common probability space or finite moments. The linked finite-space variance/covariance definition applies on one finite probability space; the general moment definition requires square-integrability. State a common probability space and square-integrability for every summand, or explicitly restrict to a finite probability space. The assigned Bernoulli example supplies a finite product space and bounded variables, so its local use is valid.

The linked CMU course copy with the same PDF filename places the variance-of-a-sum identity at Lemma 5.1.3 (PDF p. 24), while its Section 6.1 is the Lovász Local Lemma. The item needs an edition-specific locator or corrected URL. The shorter URL stored in the item did not open, so the version association is uncertain; see the [retrievable CMU copy](https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs.cmu.edu/academic/class/15850-f20/www/handouts/matousek-vondrak-prob-ln.pdf).

findings.evidence: Step 3.1 cites thm-linearity-of-expectation for E[S] = sum E[X_i], but that theorem is stated only for a finite probability space, while this lemma permits Bernoulli variables on a general probability space. A general L¹-linearity result is present in the transitive dependency closure; cite that result instead, or state a finite-product-space hypothesis. The assigned consumer uses the Bernoulli subclaim, whose local calculation is valid.
